title: Energy of charged capacitor
notes: **Energy stored.** The work done charging a capacitor is stored as electrostatic energy U = ½CV² = Q²/2C = ½QV, where C is capacitance, Q the charge and V the potential difference.
**Energy density.** The energy per unit volume between the plates is u = ½ε₀E²; the same expression gives the energy density of any electric field in vacuum.
**Charging a capacitor.** A battery of emf V supplies energy QV while charging, but only half (½QV) is stored — the rest is dissipated as heat in the circuit resistance.
**Sharing between capacitors.** When a charged capacitor shares charge with an uncharged one, total charge is conserved but energy is lost as heat until the potentials equalise.
**Applications.** Stored capacitor energy drives camera flashes, defibrillators and pulsed lasers, where energy must be released very rapidly.
